title_en: Dream of the Red Chamber (1/20): The Stone and the Crimson Pearl Flower
note_en: Look at 就把它放在青埂峰下 "so she put it at the foot of Qinggeng Peak." The 把 construction moves the object (它) in front of the verb, and the verb must then be followed by a result or a destination, here 放在 + place. English simply says "put it somewhere"; Chinese uses 把 when an action does something definite to a specific object, so a bare 把它放 with nothing after the verb would sound unfinished.

sentences.en: The book also contains the couplet "When the false is taken for true, the true becomes false; where nothing is taken for something, something becomes nothing." It means that true and false, being and nothingness, keep turning into each other, and this "true or false" theme runs through the whole of Dream of the Red Chamber.
